body:
After reading the account, the objection and the rival, here is where I have landed. Most of the account's instruments survive, but re-sequenced. The objection is accepted where it attacks the diagnostic test, and only partly where it attacks the ordering. From the rival I keep one genuinely discriminating observation and reject its opening move. Grounds follow.

Start with a principle for choosing among the three, because they disagree mostly about what to do first. We now have four live readings of the same pattern: ambiguity about what was agreed; renegotiation about whether terms still bind after a schedule change; legitimacy, about who has standing to raise an issue; and the rival's axis, about whether the flat is a unit with obligations at all. Almost every proposed action is a bet on one of these. The spec note bets on ambiguity. The "what do you take this flat to be" conversation bets on the rival's axis. When readings are unsettled, the defensible first moves are the ones that are cheap, reversible, and informative whichever reading turns out to be true. The account's one-to-one step and the rival's separate conversations converge on the same first move, while attaching rival payloads to it. The payload can wait.

The cheapest probe has been missed by all three inputs. The objection says the material cannot distinguish the readings, and that is true of the material; it is not true of the person who was there. The reader can replay the last two or three disputes at zero conversational cost and ask what each was actually about: "I thought you meant tonight" is ambiguity; "yes, but my shift changed" is renegotiation; "why is it always you who brings this up" is legitimacy; "I'm not agreeing to rules in my own home" is the rival's axis. One caution before doing this: a semantic framing is often the socially safe surface of something else, because "that's not what we said" is much easier to say than "the deal feels off now." So even disputes that present as being about meaning should not be taken at face value. This dents the account's central claim somewhat: the reported phenomenon, later disagreement about what was agreed, is evidence for ambiguity only if the semantic argument was doing the real work, and that is precisely what the replay should check.

The replay reorders the plan rather than replacing it. If the disputes were genuinely about meaning, the account's ordering stands, with one amendment: lead with the third column, not the first. What happens when someone cannot do their slot is the part that answers schedule changes, the objection's strongest alternative, and a visible default such as a fridge rotation with an explicit swap rule ("can't do your slot: swap it in advance, don't skip it") handles ambiguity and renegotiation at once. It also partially depersonalizes enforcement, since the rule asks rather than a roommate, which speaks a little to the legitimacy reading too. If instead the disputes cluster at moments of schedule change, the swap rule is the main instrument and done-ness criteria are secondary. The account undersold its own fallback column; it read like an appendix, and it is the most hypothesis-robust element in the whole plan.

The conversation with the avoiding flatmate comes next, framed as an attempt to talk about the chores less, not more. Make the ask genuinely small, and accept "I don't care, you decide" as a real answer. It can be sincere preference-delegation, and it is diagnostic in the rival's direction. But it has a limit: delegation can cover rules about that person, not silent absorption of their tasks by the other two; otherwise resentment simply changes address. If delegation is followed by non-delivery, that instability is itself data.

From the rival I keep the reaction test and add a control it did not include. When an explicit arrangement is put on the table, watch whether the flatmate engages with its content or pulls back from the arrangement itself. But do not read immediate reaction as decisive, because pullback may be a response to the proposer and the shared history rather than to writtenness as such. Use the most neutral form available, and delay interpretation until after the next schedule change. Sustained pullback across forms and contents is the signal that points to the de-exposure designs: owned zones, split shopping, shrinking what is shared at all, including a paid cleaner if affordable. Their limits should be named. Zones suit divisible tasks, not shared-flow ones like the dishes everyone generates, and none of them touches load resentment by itself; a lopsided arrangement with zones is still lopsided.

What I reject, and why. The rival's opening move, asking each flatmate what they take the flat to be, is the heaviest conversational form available and reproduces exactly the prelude-to-settlement shape that plausibly drove the withdrawal; the rival's own shield objection concedes the misuse risk. Keep the question in the background; it may get answered inside the one-to-one conversations without ever being asked directly. I also reject the account's use of its test as a verdict. The objection is right that reduced recurrence on specified items is compatible with every reading, so no single outcome should be read as confirmation or refutation. What to look for instead is convergence: the replay, the reaction to an explicit ask, and what happens at the next schedule change.

If explicit arrangements are declined across forms and the de-exposure designs are declined too, the question is no longer about chores, and the living-arrangement question should be named once, plainly, and not forced in the same conversation. The account and the rival agree on that escalation; what I add are the intermediate rungs before it.

What stays open: which reading is right, which cannot be settled from here, and whether the withdrawal is about the household at all. It could be work stress or something outside the flat entirely, in which case every chore-side instrument misfires and the one-to-one conversation is the only probe that could show it. I would hold that possibility with the same weight as any of the four readings, and nothing in the material lets any of us rule it out.

both are compatible with the reported pattern.","scope":"Bears on how the retrospective classification in k4 should be read."},{"id":"k4","type":"use","text":"Replay the last two or three disputes privately and classify each: about what was meant (ambiguity), about whether terms still bind after a change (renegotiation), about who may raise it (legitimacy), or about whether the flat carries such rules at all (the rival's axis).","action":"Private retrospective classification before any new conversation; start no new dispute for diagnostic purposes.","consequence":"Genuinely semantic disputes reinstate the account's ordering with the fallback rule foregrounded; disputes clustering on schedule changes make the swap rule the main instrument; pressing for engagement replicates the form being avoided."},{"id":"k7","type":"objection","text":"The rival's proposed opening move, asking each flatmate what they take the flat to be, should not be used first: it is indexed to one reading, it is the heaviest available conversational form, and it reproduces the prelude-to-settlement shape that plausibly drove the withdrawal.","bearing":"Downgrades the rival's opening from first move to background question; does not reject the unit-versus-privacy reading, which k4 and k8 keep live.","grounds":"The adjudication principle in k1, plus the rival's own concession that the privacy framing can pathologize explicitness and shield non-contribution."},{"id":"k8","type":"use","text":"Use reaction to an explicit arrangement, not only its content, as data, with a control the rival did not include: present the arrangement in the most neutral form available and delay interpretation until after the next schedule change, because pullback may be a response to the proposer and the history rather than to writtenness as such.","action":"Offer the explicit arrangement in a low-stakes, neutral form; do not treat immediate reaction as decisive.","consequence":"Sustained pullback across forms and contents supports the de-exposure designs in k9; engagement with content supports the ambiguity reading and the specification route.","depends":["k4"]},{"id":"k9","type":"use","text":"If k4 and k8 point away from specification, adopt de-exposure designs: owned zones for divisible tasks, split or separate shopping, shrinking what is shared at all, including a paid cleaner if affordable, while naming their limits, since zones do not cover shared-flow chores and none of these address load resentment by themselves.","action":"Mix instruments rather than choosing one: zones for attribute-like tasks, rotation with an explicit swap rule for shared-flow tasks.","consequence":"Reduces mutual exposure at some cost in efficiency and money; if engagement is still declined even under reduced exposure, escalate per k10."},{"id":"k10","type":"commitment","text":"If explicit arrangements are declined across forms and de-exposure designs are also declined, treat the question as no longer about chores and name the living-arrangement question once, plainly, without forcing a decision in the same conversation.","scope":"Contingent on k8 and k9 both being tried and failing.","action":"Raise the lease-and-living-arrangement question explicitly, one time.","consequence":"Puts the larger decision on the table without deriving it from a chore dispute, retaining the escalations the account and rival already agreed on while adding the intermediate rungs in k9."},{"id":"k11","type":"objection","text":"The account's original test, whether two or three specified items stop recurring, should not be used as a verdict on the ambiguity reading, since reduced recurrence on specified items is compatible with all four readings.","bearing":"Weakens the account's stated consequence for its specification claim while keeping the specification instruments usable under the findings of k4; results should instead be read for convergence across k4, k8 and the next schedule change.","grounds":"Acceptance of the objection's point that the test's discriminating power is lower than the account implied; the objection also noted that recurrence may resurface as fresh complaint items or after the next change of circumstances."},{"id":"k12","type":"problem","text":"Which reading is correct remains open and cannot be settled from the exposed material; additionally, the withdrawal may be about something outside the household entirely, in which case every chore-side instrument misfires and the one-to-one conversation in k6 is the only probe that could reveal it.","mentions":["k4","k6"]}],"uptake":["k1","k4","k5","k6","k8","k9","k10","k11","k12"]}
